0.content: In the Archon War, Morax defeated the god who had enslaved Xiao, freed him and named him: "Xiao" is the name of a spirit from another land's fables who endured great suffering, as he had. Xiao has served Liyue ever since to repay that debt and will not forgive anyone who speaks against Rex Lapis. When the Traveler told him of Rex Lapis's "death" in 1.0, he said he could not imagine a Liyue without him, but went to rally the other adepti anyway: "Our god is the God of Contracts after all."

1.comment: Xiao: The flute on the wind
1.content: Once, after fighting from dusk until dawn, Xiao collapsed as the gods' hatred overwhelmed him. Then the pain vanished: a clear flute melody, carried over mountains and rivers on the wind, played until first light and gave him a moment's peace. He did not seek the player, already half-sure who it must be, since only one of The Seven could help him. The official Yakshas teaser shows Venti playing. Xiao's own line about Venti ("So that's the name he goes by. His tunes are... forget it.") shows he knows who Venti really is.

2.content: The yakshas were fierce illuminated beasts whom Morax called on to purge plagues, curses and miasmas spawned by the defeated gods. Five were foremost: Bosacius (the eldest and their leader), Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus. Their work fed karmic debt into their souls; some succumbed to rage or madness, some turned on each other, some vanished. Bonanus, Indarias and Menogias died, and Bosacius grew weary, left his treasures in Minlin and disappeared. Only Xiao remains.

3.content: In his Story Quest (1.3), monsters near Wangshu Inn mutated because of Xiao's accumulated karma. He admitted his karma had caused the trouble, then cleansed the Karma-Heavy Cavern with the Bane of All Evil. A fake adeptus, "Starsnatcher", was drawing more demons with a Sigil of Permission, so Xiao used the Dream Trawler art to summon his soul into a dream. The Traveler collected a censer and lamps from a shrine guarded by the spirit of Pervases, a junior yaksha who sent Xiao his regards and missed Grilled Tiger Fish. Starsnatcher turned out to be Wang Ping'an, a folklorist's grandson and a fan of the Vigilant Yaksha, and he swore to reform. Xiao then ordered Grilled Tiger Fish instead of Almond Tofu, in honour of his old friend.

4.content: The Qixing built Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh as a base for Xiao; Verr Goldet and Huai'an, who run it, are Qixing agents who support him. He stops by for Almond Tofu, the one human food he can stomach, whose texture recalls the dreams he once ate. Verr Goldet says he is seldom in a good enough mood to see anyone, and she has never seen him smile. He left a harmless ghost, Dusky Ming, in their care until she can move on. The staff quietly cover for damage when his night-time battles shake the inn.

5.content: By slaughtering the endless manifestations of the vengeful gods, Xiao shattered their hatred into fragments that tainted his own soul. The resulting karmic debt can consume flesh, bone and soul. He hears the voices of the dead constantly, demanding more death. It also spreads: it mutates nearby monsters and is dangerous to mortals, whose souls are weaker than adepti's. That is why he avoids people. Mortal medicine has no effect on it.

6.comment: Xiao: The Traveler and "speak my name"
6.content: Xiao first told the Traveler to leave: mortal blood cannot bear so much adeptal energy. He softened after they helped him again and again. His standing promise is that if they are in danger they should speak his name and he will come. He says the bond between them is now too strong to sever, that he would like to know more about them, and that if the darkness ever took them, ending it would fall to him.

7.comment: Xiao: Lantern Rite and the Nuo Dance
7.content: Many Liyue festivals began as imitations of the adepti's victories over man-eating monsters. The buried gods' hatred erupts hardest during the Lantern Rite, so Xiao fights day and night throughout it with the "Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering". That is why he hates the festival, even as the lanterns rising over the safe harbor stir something in him he cannot name.
